page: The UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL4 is a KVM-hypervised server configured with 16 shared AMD EPYC 9575F vCPUs operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, requiring external storage configurations.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance is strong in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is also strong, while write bandwidth and database operations fall into the average tier. For AI workloads, LLM inference text generation using a small 135M model achieves top-tier speeds, though prompt processing remains in the average tier.

The server offers high resource density with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated GPU acceleration, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive and GPU-accelerated tasks. However, the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent key architectural tradeoffs that require external storage solutions and may introduce resource contention. This configuration is suited for light LLM inference, image processing, text processing, and GPU-accelerated data science tasks.
